descricao_original: A view of the stone terraces that constitute the artificial stone platform at the centre of Khami World Heritage Site near Bulawayo. Built from granite blocks and with out cement, i.e dry stone walling, it would have been the residence of main members of the Royal elite of the Torwa or Butua State - a centralised political entity that arose in southwestern Zimbabwe after the decline of the Great Zimbabwe State. Probably dates to between fifteenth to seventeenth centuries.
